### Archrock to Acquire HiVolt Energy Holdings, LLC


November 10, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s26.q4cdn.com/362558937/files/doc_news/2026/Nov/10/AROC-HiVolt-Press-Release.pdf)


- Combines HiVolt’s proven, differentiated prime power microgrid infrastructure platform – comprising vertically integrated development, ownership and operations across power generation, battery energy storage systems, fuel pipelines and private-line infrastructure that delivers reliable, utility-grade power – with Archrock’s leading compression capabilities
- Expands offerings for new and existing oil and gas customers through complementary prime power microgrid solutions supported by long-term power purchase agreements, with upside from future industrial markets
- Transaction expected to be immediately accretive to earnings per share and cash available for dividend per share
- $415 million upfront purchase price plus the portion of the earnout paid through 2028 represents a transaction multiple of approximately 6.1x the midpoint of HiVolt’s expected 2028 adjusted EBITDA range of $70–75 million, approximately 70% of which is supported by operating and contracted and awarded opportunities that provide strong visibility into expected earnings
- Archrock to host a conference call at 5:30 PM ET


HOUSTON and MIDLAND, Texas, Nov. 10, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Archrock, Inc. (NYSE: AROC) (“Archrock”) and HiVolt Energy Holdings, LLC (“HiVolt”) today announced that they have entered into a definitive merger agreement under which Archrock will acquire HiVolt in an all-cash transaction with an aggregate value of up to $450 million. The purchase price includes a payment of $415 million in cash at close plus $35 million of earnout incentives based on the achievement of certain commercial milestones.


“Combining HiVolt’s proven prime power microgrid platform with Archrock's natural gas compression offerings will transform our company into a broader provider of energy infrastructure,” said Brad Childers, President and Chief Executive Officer of Archrock. “HiVolt has built a proven, differentiated platform in the energy microgrid market that complements our core compression business and will enable us to provide additional essential services to customers across the energy value chain, particularly in power-constrained geographies. The transaction also offers upside from future industrial markets. We are confident that this transaction will advance our strategic priorities and drive long-term growth and value creation for Archrock shareholders.”


Childers continued, “A key part of what makes HiVolt such an exciting addition to Archrock is its talent. HiVolt’s highly experienced people bring deep expertise and a proven track record in developing, operating and scaling distributed power infrastructure using high-quality Caterpillar equipment. We look forward to welcoming HiVolt CEO Josh Evans and the HiVolt team to Archrock and working together to deliver on the substantial opportunities ahead.”


**Compelling Strategic and Financial Benefits**


- **Broadens Archrock’s energy infrastructure capabilities with an integrated portfolio of compression and prime power microgrid offerings:** The transaction combines mutually supportive businesses with comparable capital, return and operating characteristics, establishing Archrock in the attractive power generation sector while building on its proven compression platform. HiVolt’s behind-the-meter prime power generation, battery energy storage systems, fuel gas pipelines, private-line infrastructure and operating capabilities complement Archrock’s leading natural gas compression platform, including its established position as a leader in electric motor-drive compression. Given the strong customer overlap, bringing these capabilities into one integrated portfolio will provide Archrock with significant opportunities to deepen and extend relationships, cross-sell offerings and support a broader portion of the energy value chain.
- **Adds recurring cash flows and compelling risk-adjusted returns through long-term power purchase agreements:** HiVolt has over 80 megawatts of contracted prime power capacity today, with significant near-term contracting opportunities, providing an established earnings base with significant runway for growth. This capacity is supported by long-term, take-or-pay style, capacity-based power purchase agreements with an initial duration of five to eight years. This attractive structure creates infrastructure-quality revenue streams with strong visibility and growth potential.
- **Contracted procurement framework supports growth:** HiVolt has sufficient equipment on order to deliver forecasted growth for 2028. The company has secured access to more than 500 megawatts of near-term generation equipment using high-quality Caterpillar engines, exceeding forecast requirements and supporting further growth.
- **Accretive to earnings per share and cash available for dividend per share:** Expected to be immediately accretive to Archrock’s earnings per share and cash available for dividend per share.
- **Provides exposure to attractive prime power microgrid growth:** HiVolt’s pipeline of prime power microgrid opportunities positions Archrock to expand its role in the oil and gas value chain, with upside from future industrial markets.


**Transaction, Leadership and Closing Details**


Under the terms of the agreement, Archrock intends to fund the upfront $415 million cash portion of the total transaction consideration with available capacity under its ABL credit facility. The transaction is expected to be debt-free, resulting in pro forma leverage that is consistent with Archrock’s stated target range of between 3.0 times and 3.5 times. The $415 million upfront purchase price plus the portion of the earnout paid through 2028 represents a transaction multiple of approximately 6.1x the midpoint of HiVolt’s expected 2028 adjusted EBITDA range of $70–75 million, approximately 70% of which is supported by operating and contracted and awarded opportunities, providing strong visibility into expected earnings.


The transaction has been unanimously approved by the Board of Directors of Archrock and is expected to close in early 2027, subject to regulatory approval and other customary closing conditions.


Following close of the transaction, HiVolt will operate as a separate business segment within Archrock and continue to be led by Josh Evans. Archrock is committed to maintaining HiVolt’s organization, personnel and operations, as well as its presence in Midland, Texas, while expanding HiVolt’s footprint nationwide.

**Advisors**


Evercore is serving as financial advisor and Norton Rose Fulbright US LLP is acting as legal advisor to Archrock. BofA Securities is serving as financial advisor and Troutman Pepper Locke LLP is acting as legal advisor to HiVolt.


**About Archrock**


Archrock is an energy infrastructure company with a primary focus on midstream natural gas compression and a commitment to helping its customers produce, compress and transport natural gas in a safe and environmentally responsible way. Headquartered in Houston, Texas, Archrock is a premier provider of natural gas compression services to customers in the energy industry throughout the U.S. and a leading supplier of aftermarket services to customers that own compression equipment. For more information on how Archrock embodies its purpose, WE POWER A CLEANER AMERICA®, visit[www.archrock.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=KgLw8Myrafa4Nj4WvAEJVaBd52djmRgKIJDNO3241fqNUy3u-p3ewKQ8FYADA6IVAooUWiwnO_5PyCqq9ll4n91atQYgE-dnVTEiAIKUBSE=) .


**About HiVolt**


Founded in 2019, HiVolt Energy was created for customers who need more than a temporary power solution but don’t have the luxury of time to wait for the grid to arrive. HiVolt offers prime power solutions focused on industrial and commercial businesses with long-term base-load power needs, delivering systems that are highly reliable, regulatory-compliant, environmentally conscious, efficient, and tailored to meet end-user load demands. Designed and operated by an experienced, solution-focused team, HiVolt works directly with equipment manufacturers and technology partners to build systems capable of continuous, prime power operations. For more information, visit[hivoltenergy.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=SQmVqEBXZiZ7IwBA4UVvVGEXvdC0xRsY5owwwcBOuJ6ZOdAilpScCUvEOjkOJtjZlYs9oAkfzw5CmtX-XFsDT9CTrQIHxMy56q6I2hgD498=) .

**Non-GAAP Measures**


Adjusted EBITDA, a non-GAAP measure, is defined as net income (loss) excluding interest expense, income taxes, depreciation and amortization, long-lived and other asset impairment, unrealized change in fair value of investment in unconsolidated affiliate, restructuring charges, debt extinguishment loss, transaction-related costs, non-cash stock-based compensation expense, amortization of capitalized implementation costs and other items. Archrock has not provided projected net income from the assets to be acquired, the most comparable financial measure calculated in accordance with GAAP, or a reconciliation of projected adjusted EBITDA to projected net income of the assets to be acquired. Archrock does not control the assets to be acquired or prepare the related financial statements. Archrock is unable to provide projected net income of the assets to be acquired or a reconciliation of the projected adjusted EBITDA of the assets to be acquired to projected net income from those assets because the calculation of projected adjusted EBITDA was based on, among other things, projected utilization and rate information combined with high-level, operating expense assumptions related to the assets to be acquired. As such, Archrock does not have sufficient information to project net income from the assets to be acquired, nor does Archrock have sufficient information regarding all of the reconciling items that may exist between projected adjusted EBITDA and projected net income for the assets to be acquired. Therefore, projected net income of the assets to be acquired and a reconciliation of projected adjusted EBITDA of the assets to projected net income from those assets are not available without unreasonable effort.
